machine: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, Intel Core Ultra 7 255H (16 cores), integrated Intel graphics, 16 GB RAM
source: generated testsrc2 1920x1080 30 fps H.264, GOP 250 (8.33 s), 180 s
test: tests/CutCap.Interop.Tests/ThumbnailTests.cs MeasurePlaybackStartupWhileThumbnailsDecode (explicit; real ABI 8 engine, real FFmpeg 9.0.1; Debug engine DLL)
method: Timeline Play -> state Playing. (a) Warm session, cold start at each position (a distant seek first); each position measured idle and with a 6-sample thumbnail batch in flight, alternating which runs first. (b) First play of a fresh engine session at 5 s, idle versus busy, alternated. Per-input -threads 1 in effect. Second run of the test (the first run's warm pairs agreed within 230 ms).
conclusion: No measurable start-up penalty from a concurrent thumbnail batch: warm pairs differ by -99..+241 ms with no consistent sign, and first plays of fresh sessions at 5 s take 2.18-2.34 s either way. Start-up is dominated by the decode distance from the previous keyframe (0.8-3.8 s on this GOP-250 source). Steady-state timeline playback while thumbnails decode copied 30.0 fps with 0 dropped frames (native trace).

batch_cpu_before_and_after_thread_fix.command: 6 keyframe-seeked samples, 1080p GOP 250, 114x64 RGBA, three runs each
batch_cpu_before_and_after_thread_fix.note: -threads is a per-input decoder option; given once it applied to the first input only, so a batch used ~2.7 cores on average. Per input it uses ~1.1 cores (below-normal priority) at the cost of ~2x batch wall time.
